title: AI collections: can it help collectors recover more within the rules?
description: AI collections for community banks, credit unions and lenders: what AI ranks and drafts, what collectors keep, the contact rules and real usage costs.
industry: community banks, credit unions and specialty lenders
verdict: Let AI rank overdue accounts, time each contact and draft messages. Collectors keep the hard conversations.[^1][^2]
AI-only calling collected less than people in a 22-million-case study. Hand accounts to collectors early.[^1][^3]
Regulation F covers outside debt collectors. Your own loans still face unfair-practice, robocall and state collection laws.[^4][^5]
Two of 11 vendors we checked publish a price. None backs its results with independent evidence.[^6][^7]
Start with reminders on early-stage accounts, tested against today's strategy on a random half.[^8][^9]

headings.human-role: Which collections decisions stay with your people?
headings.team-after: What do collectors do once AI takes the first pass?
headings.example: What does AI do with one overdue loan?
headings.something-else: When should a collections team pick something else?

summary: AI for collections is software that ranks overdue loans, picks when and how to reach each borrower, and drafts the message.[^10][^2] What changes: collectors stop dialling cold and spend their day on hardship cases, high balances and escalations.[^1][^2] Contact limits, consent and hand-offs to people must be built in.[^11][^12]

answers.human-role: Your collectors and managers keep every decision that changes what a borrower owes or stops contact: bankruptcy and military matches, hardship plans, disputes and message templates.[^13][^14][^16]
answers.team-after: Collectors spend their day on hardship cases, high balances, escalations and borrowers AI could not reach, instead of dialling cold.[^1][^2]
answers.example: On a 34-day-late auto loan, AI ranks it as likely to cure, schedules a 6:30pm text with a payment link, and holds the draft for a collector's approval.[^24][^11]
answers.recipes: Most firms should turn on the AI in the collections system they already run. Add usage-priced reminders for many small early accounts, and build only with a data team.[^27][^8][^42]
answers.rules: A lender collecting its own loans faces unfair-practice law (UDAAP), the TCPA for calls and texts, and state collection laws. Regulation F mainly binds outside collectors.[^5][^48][^4] Bankruptcy, military, fair-lending and credit-dispute rules apply either way.[^14][^15]
answers.benchmark: Run the AI on a random share of accounts and today's strategy on the rest, then compare cures, roll rates, complaints and opt-outs after 90 days.[^10][^42][^36]
answers.what-goes-wrong: AI for collections goes wrong when it deals with borrowers alone: AI-only calls collect less, and missing consent, stacked contacts, threatening drafts and missed refusals bring legal risk.[^1][^17][^48][^18]
answers.something-else: Pick something else when your collections system already has AI built in, the debt is charged off and belongs with an agency, or a plain reminder will do.[^27][^4][^8]

humanRole: Your people keep every decision that changes what a borrower owes or whether contact must stop. AI only ranks, times and drafts.[^12][^13]

Collections manager: confirms every bankruptcy or military-service match before anyone makes contact. A bankruptcy filing stops collection, and the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act (SCRA) caps debt taken on before service at 6% interest.[^14][^15]

Senior collector or loan officer: decides hardship plans, loan modifications and disputes. A modification counts as new credit under fair-lending rules, and credit-report disputes need an investigation.[^13][^16]

Compliance lead: approves every template and the house contact cap, your own limit per account, and samples AI calls and texts weekly. Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) examiners found over 100 calls made after people asked a collector to stop.[^17][^18]
teamAfter: Collectors spend the day on accounts that need a person: hardship, high balances and borrowers AI could not reach. When a person took over on day 6, AI's shortfall fell to 0.8 points.[^1][^3]
Collectors work escalations instead of dialling cold. One credit union reported 4% of AI conversations went to a person, mostly members who asked for one (vendor webinar).[^2]

New collectors get up to speed faster: AI help raised support agents' output 14%, and 34% for novices.[^19][^20] The Bureau of Labor Statistics expects about 11,200 collector openings a year to 2035.[^21]
Among US firms where AI changed tasks, 66% use it only to help staff and 2% report employment decreases.[^22][^23]

example.input: AI ranks the loan, picks the channel and hour, drafts the message, and holds anything a person must decide. Illustrative: an auto loan 34 days late at a 200-staff credit union. AI reads the balance, payment history, past promises, consent flags, opt-outs, time zone and bankruptcy and military checks.
example.output: The loan lands in the morning queue as "likely to cure: text at 6:30pm local with a payment link", inside the 8am-9pm window.[^24] The drafted text waits for a collector's approval, and a counter shows contacts used against the house cap.[^11] Had the bankruptcy check matched, the loan would sit on hold for the collections manager instead.[^14]

recipes.name: 1. Fits most firms (1-4 collectors): turn on the AI in the collections system you run
recipes.when: For a credit union or bank already on AKUVO, Temenos, C&R Software or a core collections module.[^27][^29] You get ranking and drafting without a new system to vet.[^43]
flow: Collections manager: list today's queues, cure rates and roll rates
IT lead: switch on the vendor's AI module for one test queue
Compliance lead: approve message templates and the house contact cap
Collector: work the AI-ranked queue and flag bad picks
Collections manager: compare cures with the old queue after 60 days
recipes.cost: Not published by AKUVO, Temenos or C&R Software, so ask for a quote on your account volume.[^28][^29][^31] Budget time for the vendor review bank regulators expect.[^43]

recipes.name: 2. Many small early-stage accounts (5-15 collectors): add usage-priced reminders and AI voice
recipes.when: For lenders with many small balances in the first 30 days late, where a timely reminder often cures the loan.[^8][^9]
flow: Data analyst: score each account for its chance to cure on its own
Compliance lead: set consent rules, quiet hours and contact caps for each state
Operations lead: send texts and AI-voice reminders only where consent is on file
Collector: take every hand-off and every account still late by day 6 to 10
Quality reviewer: check a sample of AI calls and texts each week
recipes.cost: Illustrative: 340 accounts × 3 calls × 3 minutes × $0.11 a minute is about $340 a month in voice.[^26] Texts cost $0.0083 a segment plus carrier fees, or pay on results at 1.5% of recovered plus $1 a payment.[^35][^6]

recipes.name: 3. Data team and 3+ years of history: build your own ranking and drafting
recipes.when: For lenders whose own payment history is the edge and who already have an analyst. Published studies show this ranking works when tested against the current strategy.[^42][^44]
flow: Analyst: build a model of who will pay and the best time to reach them
Model risk reviewer: validate it under your model risk policy
Collections manager: run it against today's strategy on a random half of accounts
Collector: approve each AI-drafted message before it goes out
Vendor manager: review any voice or language-model supplier as a third party
recipes.cost: Your analysts' time plus usage costs like recipe 2.[^26][^35] No source we found prices an in-house build.

ownData.note: Zavient check of homepage, product and pricing pages, 26 Nov 2026; a check passed only if a page said it in words. The rest were C&R Software, Prodigal and TrueAccord; all 11 came from search results and credit-union vendor lists, not at random.[^31][^46][^47] A vendor may cover a rule on a page we did not read.

rules.name: In short, for a lender collecting its own loans
rules.what: Unfair-practice law (UDAAP), the Telephone Consumer Protection Act (TCPA) and state collection laws apply to you.[^5][^48] Regulation F and the Fair Debt Collection Practices Act (FDCPA) mainly bind third-party collectors.[^4] Bankruptcy, military, fair-lending and credit-dispute rules apply either way.[^14][^15]

rules.name: Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.2: who is a debt collector
rules.what: A creditor's own staff collecting in the creditor's name are not debt collectors.[^4] The CFPB declined to extend the rule to first-party collectors in 2020.[^49][^50] Collect under another name and you may be covered.[^4]

rules.name: Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.14(b): 7 calls in 7 days
rules.what: At no more than 7 calls in 7 days per debt, and none within 7 days of a conversation, a collector is presumed compliant.[^11][^51] Calls plus texts and emails can still add up to harassment. Many lenders copy this cap as a house rule.[^50]

rules.name: Regulation F, 12 CFR 1006.6: times and opt-outs
rules.what: 8am to 9pm local time is presumed convenient, and a text counts when sent.[^24][^52] Each text or email must offer a simple way to opt out.[^24]

rules.name: UDAAP: CFPB Bulletin 2013-07
rules.what: A creditor collecting its own debts can still commit unfair, deceptive or abusive acts.[^5] Navy Federal's false threats cost about $23M in refunds and a $5.5M penalty.[^18][^53]

rules.name: TCPA: FCC ruling 24-17 on AI voices
rules.what: An AI-generated voice is an artificial voice under the TCPA.[^48][^54] Calls using one to a cell phone need the borrower's prior express consent.[^48][^55]

rules.name: TCPA: 47 USC 227 and 47 CFR 64.1200
rules.what: Borrowers can sue for $500 a violation, up to three times that if willful.[^56] Non-marketing artificial-voice calls to a home line are capped at 3 in 30 days.[^57]

rules.name: TCPA: FCC 26-67 on revoking consent
rules.status: In force from 25 Nov 2026; more changes proposed
rules.what: You may set one way to revoke, revocation can cover a category of calls, and you must honour it within 10 business days.[^58] A further proposal would shorten that window and allow "revoke all".[^59]

rules.name: Massachusetts, 940 CMR 7.04(1)(f)
rules.what: No more than 2 calls, texts or recorded messages in 7 days per debt to a borrower's home or cell phone.[^60] It applies to original creditors, not only agencies.[^61]

rules.name: California Rosenthal Act
rules.what: It brings FDCPA-style conduct rules to creditors collecting their own consumer debts.[^62]

rules.name: Bankruptcy automatic stay, 11 USC 362
rules.what: A filing stops collection at once, so check new filings daily before any contact goes out.[^14]

rules.name: SCRA interest cap, 50 USC 3937
rules.what: Debt taken on before service is capped at 6% interest during service, once the borrower sends notice and orders.[^15][^63]

rules.name: Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA): loan modifications
rules.what: CFPB exam procedures treat a modification as an extension of credit, so fair-lending rules apply.[^13] Keep modification decisions with a person.

rules.name: Fair Credit Reporting Act: direct disputes, 12 CFR 1022.43
rules.what: You must investigate qualifying credit-report disputes a borrower sends you directly.[^16]

rules.name: New York City automated customer service rules
rules.what: If adopted, they would require AI disclosure at the start and a one-step transfer to a person.[^64] Penalties would run up to $3,500.[^64]

howToTest: Test it side by side: AI on a random share of accounts, today's strategy on the rest, compared after 90 days.[^10][^42]
Pull your last 90 days of numbers from your system, so there is no wait. Track roll rate (share moving from 30 to 60 days late), cures, promises kept, complaints and opt-outs.[^36][^37]
Pilot one product, such as auto loans, in its first 30 days late. AI's shortfall in the 22-million-case study peaked about a month in.[^1]
Write the hand-off rule before launch: any account not cured by day 6 to 10 goes to a collector.[^1]
Count every call, text and email against one house cap. Regulators judge total contact, not one channel.[^11][^17]
Script 20 or more ways people say stop, bankruptcy, deployed or not my debt. Check each one stops contact or reaches a person.[^17][^65]
Sample AI calls and drafted messages weekly for false or threatening statements.[^18][^53]
Price the lift: extra cures × average balance × your charge-off rate, minus usage cost. The credit union average charge-off rate is 0.78%.[^36]
Treat rising complaints or opt-outs as a stop signal, even if recoveries rise.[^66][^17]
watchOuts: It goes wrong where AI deals with borrowers alone: AI-only calls, missing consent, stacked contacts, threatening drafts and missed refusals.[^1][^17]
AI-only calling collects less: 9% less at 30 days and 21% fewer promises to pay. Hand off to people early.[^1][^3]

AI voices without consent: the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) treats them as artificial voices, at $500 a call, tripled if willful. Check consent per number and the reassigned-numbers database first.[^48][^56][^67]
Contacts stacking across channels: Massachusetts allows creditors 2 calls or texts a week per debt. Run one counter across calls, texts and emails, set to your strictest state.[^60][^11]
Drafts that threaten: Navy Federal's letters implied legal action and cost about $23M in refunds plus a $5.5M penalty. Have compliance approve every template.[^18][^53]
Bots that trap people or miss a refusal: the CFPB warns chatbots that block human help can break the law. Test a one-step route to a person monthly.[^12][^65]

faq.q: Does Regulation F apply when a bank or credit union collects its own loans?
faq.a: Generally no: it excludes a creditor's own staff collecting in the creditor's name.[^4][^49] Unfair-practice law, the TCPA and state laws still apply, and many lenders copy Regulation F's limits anyway.[^5][^50]

faq.q: Can AI replace human debt collectors?
faq.a: Not on current evidence: in 22 million cases, AI callers collected less than people, and handing off early closed most of the gap.[^1][^3]
Yes, on routine reminders and first contacts. One credit union reported only 4% of AI conversations needed a person (vendor webinar).[^2] Plain email and text reminders also cut late payment.[^8][^9]

faq.q: Do we need consent to use an AI voice?
faq.a: Yes, for calls to cell phones. The FCC treats AI voices as artificial voices under the TCPA.[^48][^55] Some credit unions add consent language to the membership agreement (vendor webinar).[^2]

faq.q: How are AI collections tools priced?
faq.a: AI collections tools charge by monthly voice minutes ($99 to $4,999)[^7], by a share of what they recover (1.5%)[^6], or per call minute or text.[^26][^35] Voice building blocks run $0.07 to $0.31 a minute, and texts about $0.0083 each.[^26][^35] Nine of the 11 vendors we checked publish no price.[^6][^7]

faq.q: Who handles hardship and disputes when AI is in the loop?
faq.a: A person, every time, because a loan modification counts as new credit under fair-lending rules and credit-report disputes need an investigation.[^13][^16]

buyVsBuild.buy: Usually buy first, when your collections system offers an AI module, you have no data team and your strategy is standard.[^27][^29] Most enterprise AI spend now goes to bought apps.[^68] A bought tool still needs a third-party risk review.[^43]
buyVsBuild.build: Build the ranking and rules layer when your payment history is the edge or you collect across states with different caps.[^60][^62] Bought tools from specialist vendors succeed more often than internal builds, so build only with a named owner.[^69]

pickElse: Pick something else when your system already has AI built in, the debt belongs with an agency, or a plain reminder will do.[^27][^8]
Already on AKUVO, Temenos or C&R Software: try that platform's own AI module before adding a new vendor.[^27][^29][^31]
Charged-off debt past your own recovery stage: a licensed collection agency such as TrueAccord, which must follow Regulation F.[^4][^47]
Early, low-balance accounts: autopay enrolment and plain text or email reminders, which cut late payment without AI.[^8][^9]

offer.heading: Which overdue accounts should AI touch first?
offer.body: Usually your early-stage, low-balance accounts, and we can check yours in a free 30-minute call. Bring 90 days of delinquency buckets and contact counts. You leave with the first step, a side-by-side test plan and a before-and-after measure.

sources.what: How community banks should vet and oversee vendors, including technology suppliers.

sources.what: Learns a collections policy offline from logged contacts and compares it with the logged policy.

sources.name: Salient, homepage
sources.what: Names FDCPA, TCPA and CFPB; says no human review is required on every call; no price (read 26 Nov 2026).

sources.name: Prodigal, homepage
sources.what: Says "fully compliant" without naming rules; no price; payment and agent claims (vendor claims; read 26 Nov 2026).

sources.name: TrueAccord, homepage
sources.what: A collection agency, not software; "AI + Human" model; no price (vendor claims; read 26 Nov 2026).

sources.name: FCC, Declaratory Ruling FCC 24-17 (Feb 2024)
sources.what: Calls using AI-generated voices are calls using an artificial voice under the TCPA, so consent rules apply.

sources.name: Consumer Finance Monitor (Ballard Spahr), the CFPB final debt collection rule's impacts on creditors (3 Nov 2020)
sources.what: The CFPB declined to extend Regulation F to first-party collectors.

sources.name: American Bar Association, Business Law Today: six things creditors should know about the debt collection rule (Jan 2021)
sources.what: Creditors are mostly outside Regulation F; many adopt its limits as a standard anyway.

sources.name: eCFR, 12 CFR 1006.14
sources.what: Official text of the Regulation F call-frequency presumption.

sources.name: eCFR, 12 CFR 1006.6
sources.what: Official text of the Regulation F rules on inconvenient times and electronic opt-outs.

sources.name: CFPB, Navy Federal Credit Union consent order (2016)
sources.what: Letters implied legal action and contacting commanding officers; about 700,000 accounts were frozen.

sources.name: FCC, FCC confirms the TCPA applies to AI technologies that generate human voices
sources.what: Announcement of the AI-voice ruling.

sources.name: FCC, robocall rules for callers (updated 17 Nov 2026)
sources.what: Plain-English consent and revocation rules for callers.

sources.name: US Code, 47 USC 227 (TCPA)
sources.what: Private right of action for $500 per violation, up to three times that if willful or knowing.

sources.name: eCFR, 47 CFR 64.1200: delivery restrictions
sources.what: Consent rules for artificial-voice calls; exempt non-telemarketing calls to residential lines are limited to 3 in 30 days.

sources.name: Federal Register, FCC 26-67 final rule on revoking consent (26 Oct 2026)
sources.what: Effective 25 Nov 2026: callers may set an exclusive revocation method, revocation can be by category, and must be honoured within 10 business days.

sources.name: Federal Register, FCC further notice of proposed rulemaking on revocation (26 Oct 2026)
sources.what: Proposes, not yet final: faster honouring windows and a single "revoke all".

sources.name: 940 CMR 7.04, Massachusetts debt collection regulations (Cornell LII)
sources.what: A creditor may not initiate more than 2 calls in 7 days to a debtor's residence, cell phone or other personal number per debt.

sources.name: Mass.gov, fair debt collection
sources.what: Massachusetts debt collection regulations apply to original creditors as well as collection agencies.

sources.name: California Civil Code, Rosenthal Fair Debt Collection Practices Act
sources.what: Defines debt collectors to include creditors collecting their own consumer debts.

sources.name: CFPB, the Servicemembers Civil Relief Act
sources.what: Plain-English SCRA protections, including the 6% cap.

sources.name: Consumer Finance Monitor (Ballard Spahr), New York City proposes rules for automated customer service systems (26 Oct 2026)
sources.what: Proposed rules, not final: AI disclosure at the start, one-step transfer to a person, 3-year records, penalties up to $3,500; hearing held 19 Nov 2026.

sources.name: Consumer Finance Monitor podcast, AI in debt collection (24 Sep 2026)
sources.what: Consumer-facing AI must recognise informal refusals to pay as requests to stop; voice bots carry TCPA risk.

sources.name: CFPB, Fair Debt Collection Practices Act annual report 2025
sources.what: Complaints can name first-party collectors; complaints about institutions of $10 billion or less go to their prudential regulator.

sources.name: FCC, Reassigned Numbers Database
sources.what: Checking the database gives a safe harbour for calls to numbers that changed hands.

sources.name: Menlo Ventures, 2025: The State of Generative AI in the Enterprise
sources.what: Most enterprise generative AI spend goes to bought applications rather than internal builds.

sources.name: Fortune, MIT report: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing (18 Aug 2025)
sources.what: Fortune's write-up of MIT NANDA's The GenAI Divide report. Headline: 95% of generative AI pilots at companies are failing; about 5% of AI pilot programs achieve rapid revenue acceleration, while the vast majority stall with little to no measurable P&L impact. Purchasing AI tools from specialized vendors and building partnerships succeed about 67% of the time. Its comparison for internal builds misstates the report, where internal builds reach deployment about a third of the time: cite this write-up for the 67% and its headline figures only; MIT's report carries the internal-build rate and the "twice" comparison. Read 28 Nov 2026.

reviews.notes: Dana, as COO of a 200-staff credit union: the bottom line names the first step, and every recipe step names who does it. The test plan made her wait 90 days for a baseline before a 90-day trial; it now pulls the last 90 days from the system, so a pilot can start at once. 'Roll rate' was jargon and is now defined in the step.

Head of collections operations, reading on a phone: the rules table ran to 16 rows, so the FDIC vendor-guide row was cut (vendor review stays in recipes and buy-or-build). 'House contact cap' was used before it was explained; the compliance bullet now defines it. Tools table kept at 10 rows because each row carries a price or 'not published'.

A GM running a region asked whether one branch or product can pilot and what it does to margin. The test now starts with one product, such as auto loans, in its first 30 days late. Margin is priced in the lift step (extra cures times balance times charge-off rate, minus usage) and in recipe 2's illustrative $340 a month; no sourced lift figure for a lender this size exists, so none is given.

Head of collections at a community bank, checking the law: the Regulation F row said 'under 7 calls', which misstates the presumption; it now reads 'no more than 7'. Massachusetts counts texts and recorded messages too, so its row and watch-out now say so. The TCPA 3-in-30 line now says non-marketing calls, and the SCRA line says debt taken on before service. First-party scope is stated once, sourced to the CFPB, with UDAAP, TCPA and state law named as what still applies.

Steve gets the answer in the title and bottom line in 10 seconds and sees what vendors charge or that they don't publish. 'Champion-challenger' was jargon at the top; it is now a side-by-side test on your own accounts, in On this page, the test steps and the offer. Security has no collections-specific source in the research, so it is covered as the vendor review in recipes and buy-or-build. All mid-size results are vendor claims and say so; no independent case from a lender his size exists.
